newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court rejects O'Dell appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court rejects O'Dell appeal.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected an appeal by convicted rapist and murderer Joseph O'Dell, clearing the way for his execution in Virginia by lethal injection later in the night.

The high court denied a request by the death-row inmate whose case drew protests from Italy and the Vatican. The court's 9-0 vote allowed state authorities to proceed with the scheduled exeecution of O'Dell at 9 p.m. EDT (0100 GMT Thursday) for the 1985 rape and murder of Helen Schartner of Virginia Beach.

Virginia Gov. George Allen also denied O'Dell's last-minute plea for clemency, and a federal appeals court in Richmond turned down a request for new DNA tests on behalf of O'Dell, saying the claim was "meritless," the Virginia Attorney General's Office said.

"After a painstaking, careful and thorough review of all the evidence and information available to me, I see no legitimate reason that would justify my overturning the judgment of the jury and judge who heard this case," Allen said in a five-page statement released late on Wednesday.

Allen denied that his decision to deny clemency to O'Dell was about vengeance. "It is about justice and accountability," Allen said in the statement, adding that he hoped O'Dell would find peace with God before his execution.
In their Supreme Court appeal, O'Dell's lawyers argued that state-of-the-art testing of sperm and semen samples recovered from the victim's body could conclusively prove his innocence.

But state lawyers replied that O'Dell's conviction and death sentence were upheld in countless legal proceedings, including a Supreme Court ruling in June. "O'Dell's last-minute claim must be rejected as abusive, frivolous and insufficient," Assistant Attorney General Katherine Baldwin said.
O'Dell, 55, was married to his volunteer paralegal, Lori Urs, 41, in a midday wedding on Wednesday at the Greenville Correction Centre, prison spokesman David Botkins said.

O'Dell remained behind bars and the couple was not allowed to touch. The ceremony was conducted by the Rev. Russell Ford, a former prison chaplain who has known O'Dell for many years. It was O'Dell's fourth marriage, Urs' second.
As his wife, Urs will be entitled to claim his body from the Virginia State Medical Examiner's Office.
Italian interest in the O'Dell case has bewildered and annoyed Schartner's family. "It's just like the Italians hate us," her sister, Gail Lee, told the Norfolk Virginian Pilot newspaper.

"I used to have great respect for that country and its history and its art ... now I never want to go there. I never want to set foot on their soil. Because by listening to just one side of this case, they in essence have said to my family, 'You are worthless. Helen's life didn't matter.'"
The pope and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi appealed to halt the execution of O'Dell, who has a long criminal record and no known ties to Italy.
O'Dell was made an honorary citizen of the city of Palermo and has said he wanted to be buried there.
Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the most vocal supporters of a worldwide ban on capital punishment.
